title: Leo Louis Lion and the Sky That Turned to Smoke
vol: A Mommy Is Human Too Story · Leo Louis Lion
verse: The earth is our home, and taking care of it is everyone's job. Big changes start with small steps, together.

pages.text: Leo Louis Lion and the Sky That Turned to Smoke

Leo Louis Lion woke up to a strange gray sky.
Not a rain sky. Not a night sky. A smoky sky.
"Mama," he said, "the sky looks sick."

Mama Lion looked up a long, long time.
"You know what, little one?" she said. "I don't know everything about that sky.
But I know how to find out. And I know we can do it together."

So they went to see. The smoke wasn't coming from their home.
It was coming from far, far away — from forests so dry they had caught fire.
"But it's not even hot here," said Leo.
"That's the thing," said Mama. "The smoke traveled all this way to visit us."

Leo took a breath. It felt scratchy.
"The air has tiny bits of ash in it," Mama said. "That's what makes it hard to breathe.
So today we play close to home, Leo."

"But why, Mama? Why did the forests get so dry?"
Mama sat down beside him. "Now that," she said, "is a very big question.
And big questions deserve a real answer."

"The whole earth wears a blanket," said Mama. "A blanket made of air.
A little blanket keeps us just warm enough. That's a good thing."

"But when the world burns too much — too many fires, too many engines, all day and all night —
the blanket grows thicker and thicker. And a blanket too thick makes the whole earth too warm."

"When it stays too warm for too long, the rain stays away. The grass turns brown.
The trees get thirsty and dry. And dry forests catch fire easily."
Leo's eyes went wide. "So the smoke… came from the blanket?"

"In a way," said Mama. Then she was quiet a moment.
"The truth is, Leo, I didn't always know this. I learned it little by little.
Grown-ups are still learning, too."

"Then what can we do?" asked Leo. "We're just lions."
Mama smiled. "Two things. We can slow the fuel — burn less, waste less, walk more.
And we can grow the trees — because trees drink in the heavy air and help the blanket get light again."

Leo looked up at the gray sky again. "Mama… will it be all fixed tomorrow?"
Mama took a long, slow breath.
She did not want to tell him anything that wasn't true.

"Here is the truest thing I know," she said. "A long time ago, the sky had a different hurt.
And all the animals of all the lands looked up, and saw it, and said, 'Enough. Let's fix it together.'
And do you know what happened? The sky began to heal."

"So no, Leo, I cannot promise you tomorrow. But I can tell you how good things happen.
Not by one lion. By many lions, deciding together, and then doing something about it."

Leo Louis Lion lifted his chin — steady, like the name he was given.
"Then I'll tell the others," he said. "I'll teach every cub I know."
Mama's heart went full. "That," she said, "is exactly how."

And so they did. One seed. One lesson.
One brave young lion, teaching the next.
The earth is a gift. We were given it to keep.
